explanation: Choose independently whether to retain each occurrence. A lambda filter expresses this decision without changing the input or sorting the retained elements. A uniform subset is not a uniformly chosen size followed by a uniform subset of that size: sizes near n/2 correspond to more subsets and must occur more often. C++ std::copy_if uses a lambda capturing the supplied coin by reference and a back_insert_iterator into a new vector. It preserves traversal order and copies selected values without retaining the source or mutating the const input vector.
correctness: For any fixed occurrence subset S, a run returns S precisely when the independent coin for each of its members is true and the coin for every other occurrence is false. There are n required coin outcomes, each of probability 1/2, so their joint probability is 2^-n for every S. Filtering visits occurrences in input order and emits only retained values, preserving the required relative order and multiplicities. Equal Data values do not merge coin decisions. For n=0 there is one subset, the empty subset, with probability 1.
walkthrough: For [7,7,9], label occurrences a,b,c. Coin outcomes true,false,true retain a and c and return [7,9]. There are eight equally likely occurrence subsets. Returned value array [7] has probability 2/8 because either a alone or b alone produces it; [7,7] has probability 1/8. Choosing distinct values uniformly would lose this multiplicity. The empty and full arrays each occur with probability 1/8.
timeComplexity: O(n) time, with one independent supplied-coin call per input occurrence in these implementations.
spaceComplexity: O(n) worst-case space for the concrete result and any collection-building buffers. The final result has m retained occurrences; filtering does not copy or reorder the input.
edgeCases: Empty, singleton, repeated and all-equal values; signed endpoints.
Empty/full outcomes and variable size; equal-valued occurrences remain independent.
Exact original relative order, input preservation and repeated independent invocations.
1000 input occurrences with finite source usage.
